regions.text: 原理的に不可能である。

quote.translation: All measurement is merely approximate, and to attain absolute precision is in principle impossible.

regions.text: 實驗立澄とは結局は諸現象の可測的要素の値を、出來るだけ接近した限界と限界との間に壓縮することに蹄する。

quote.translation: Experimental verification comes down in the end to compressing the value of the measurable element of phenomena between limits brought as close together as possible.

regions.text: 我々が見るものは謂はば物を入れた容器に過きない。物自身ではない。

quote.translation: What we see is, so to speak, only the container in which the thing has been put, and not the thing itself.

regions.text: きうして我々の粗維な測定方法の效力範国を越えた程度の微小の和迦知働が諸現象に内在し得る。それがすなはち因果的必然の非存在としての因果的偶然（Contingenee）でぁる。

quote.translation: A minute indeterminacy, too minute to fall within the range of validity of our crude methods of measurement, can therefore be immanent in phenomena, and this is precisely causal contingency (contingence) as the non-existence of causal necessity.

regions.text: かくしてプートルーはメレスドッビランやラエッソンによつて醤道された「自由の哲學」に偶然の概念による根柢を與へようどした。

quote.translation: In this way Boutroux sought to give the "philosophy of freedom" advocated by Maine de Biran and Ravaisson a foundation in the concept of the contingent.

regions.text: なほ、エビクロスの非決定論にあつては因果偶然と目々偶然とが同種結合をなしてゐるに反してブートルーにあつては因果偶然が目的々必然と異種結合をなしてゐる。

quote.translation: Moreover, whereas in the indeterminism of Epicurus causal contingency forms a homogeneous combination with teleological contingency, in Boutroux causal contingency forms a heterogeneous combination with teleological necessity.

regions.text: エビクロスは一方に神々の存在を承認したが他方にその神々は諸世界間（ETKoaga,intermundia）の空歳に住して自足の至麗に安んじ世界と人間とに何等の干渉をしないものと考へた。

quote.translation: Epicurus acknowledged the existence of the gods, but he thought that these gods dwell in the void between the worlds (μετακόσμια, intermundia), rest content in self-sufficient bliss, and do not interfere in any way with the world or with human beings.

regions.text: 然るにプートルーの謂はゆる「自然法則の偶然性」は畢竟宇宙の目々必然性に依存してゐる（Boutroux,Dehacontingencedesloisdetanature，90Ed,p155-157）°ブートルーは「義務の形における必然性』すなはち「必然と

quote.translation: Boutroux's so-called "contingency of the laws of nature", by contrast, depends in the end on the teleological necessity of the universe (Boutroux, De la contingence des lois de la nature, 9e éd., pp. 155-157).

quote.translation: Boutroux speaks of "necessity in the form of duty", that is, of "the end conceived as necessary", and says that in God "freedom is infinite" whilst there is at the same time "practical necessity".
